text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's cabinet will not discuss the privatisation decision on Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK) as the Prime Minister has not received answers to his previous queries on the ministries' preference for the bid by a Polish banking and insurance consortium despite the fact that South Korea's Samsung offered to pay 20 zlotys more for each share.

- The head of Poland's Main Customs Office (GUC) Mieczyslaw Nogaj has resigned and the Prime Minister has appointe former deputy head Tomasz Cecelski in his place, a cabinet official press release said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Basil Kavalsky has been appointed new regional director of the World Bank for Poland and the Baltic states.
- Standard & Poor's rating agency has awarded the BBB- credit rating to the Lodz municipality in central Poland.
- Delphi Automotive Systems, controlled by the General Motors has bought a 60 percent stake in the Krosno shock-absorber plant from the National Investment Funds (NFI) worth $30 million.

- Poland's furniture export sales reached $1.5 billion in 1996, showing a $200 million upturn from the year before. The industry's sales exceeded the revenues from Polish coal exports, a report by the wood technology institute (ITD) said.

- The Consumer and Competition Protection Office (UOKK) has fined the Polar household durables maker 50,000 zlotys for imposing minimum wholesale prices for Polar's washing machines and refrigerators on distributors, UOKK Wroclaw branch director Zbigniew Jurczyk said.

- Poland's labour costs will remain low for the next five years compared with other countries, Price Waterhouse consultancy president Jermyn Brooks said. As time goes on intellectual capital and skills of the work force will be key to the economy's competitiveness.
- Furniture spending by Polish buyers in 1996 showed a 50 percent upturn from the year before, a report by Gazeta Bankowa showed.

- The Pekpol meat processing and trading group plans to up its own products' share in the group's sales to 40 percent in the next few years and increase its share in the country's meat market to several percent, Pekpol said.
- The shareholders of the PZU Zycie life insurance firm decided to increase reserve capital with the 1996 net of 100 million zlotys at a general meeting yesterday.
- Robert Zieba and Jerzy Lenart were reappointed board members of the TUK insurance firm yesterday.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Marian Czakanski has resigned his membership in the PZU Zycie supervisory board and was replaced by Elegiusz Nowakowski, the aide to PZU SA president Jan Monkiewicz.

- Poland's communes and municipalities will invest 65 billion zlotys in modernisation and development in the next 10 years to reach the EU average infrastructure development level, the municipalities said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The shareholders of the Krakchemia retail trader have given up a previously planned share capital increase as it would result in a 1.5 million zloty tax. They decided to put 915,500 zlotys from 1996 net profit to reserve capital.
- The Bank Przemyslowo Handlowy (BPH) and Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK) have provided a development credit of 95.59 million zlotys to the Siersza power plant in Trzebinia, southern Poland.
PARKIET

- The listed Elektrim foreign trade firm will be offered to buy the Rafako boiler maker's H-series share issue of 8.07 million shares priced at 11.25 zloty each, Rafako's general shareholders meeting decided.
